items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'why' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how cool this story is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement ('WOW' energy), build excitement through each line, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. 'So what's going on?' is a genuinely puzzled, excited question. 'But scientists say that's only part of it.' gets a playful, knowing lift. 'And here's the part that proves it.' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. 'Texas.' lands as its own surprised beat after a tiny pause. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Say U.S.A. as the three letters U-S-A. Say U.S. as the two letters U-S. Pronounce 'Madrid' as 'muh-DRID', 'Seattle' as 'see-AT-ul', 'Minneapolis' as 'min-ee-AP-uh-lis'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word, every line in order; never add words of your own.
lines: Why is the U.S.A.... so much colder than Europe?
New York and Madrid sit on the same line.
But in January, New York freezes... and Madrid doesn't.
London is further north than every U.S. state except Alaska.
Most people blame the Gulf Stream: warm water heading for Europe.
But scientists say that's only part of it.
The real answer is the wind. It blows west to east.
Europe's air crosses a warm ocean.
New York's air crosses a frozen continent.
And the Rockies bend that wind... dragging Arctic air south.
Nothing blocks it, so it can reach Texas.
And here's the part that proves it.
Seattle faces the ocean... so its winters are mild, like London's.
But go inland to Minneapolis... and it's a deep freeze.
So it's not how far north you are. It's where your wind comes from.
And Madrid has just one thing to say.
So... American winter or European winter? Because honestly...
